points: When a network partition splits a system, each side can keep answering or refuse stale data, but not both.
Partitions are a fact of networks, so the real choice is what to do during one, and it is decided for each kind of data.
Amazon's Dynamo starts from never rejecting a write and derives quorums, hinted handoff and reconciliation from that rule.
Google's Spanner keeps strong consistency across the globe by paying a bounded latency and engineering the clock.

figures.label: 99.9% of reads and writes complete within 300 ms, Dynamo's SLA
TrueTime clock uncertainty is 1 to 7 ms, which a transaction waits out

prerequisiteReasons.replication: CAP takes from replication the picture of several copies of one key that can end up on opposite sides of a network split.
prerequisiteReasons.sharding: CAP takes from sharding the fact that data lives on many machines joined by a network, which is where partitions come from.

points: A CDN keeps copies of content on servers close to users, so most requests are answered nearby instead of at the origin.
It has two jobs: deciding what each edge keeps when disk space is limited, and making the misses that still reach the origin cheap.
Cloudflare found a miss costs more than the trip to the origin, because setting up the connection counts, so connection reuse matters.
Netflix owns its catalog and can predict demand, so it fills caches ahead of time instead of waiting for misses.

figures.label: 160x fewer new connections to one customer's origins
around 1,200 files stored for one episode of The Crown

prerequisiteReasons.dns: CDNs take from DNS the way a user's request is pointed at a nearby server, which is how each user lands on a close edge.
prerequisiteReasons.caching: CDNs take from caching the hit, the miss and the fill, applied to many edge copies that sit in front of one origin.

points: A circuit breaker stops a client calling a failing dependency for a while, so calls fail fast instead of piling up.
Load shedding makes an overloaded server reject some requests, lowest priority first, so the rest are served in time.
Zalando's analysis of one incident found that a breaker's probes test the service at a trickle, not under the load that returns when it closes.
Uber's Cinnamon lets a server protect itself, without help from callers, by ranking requests and shedding the lowest first.

figures.label: 10x the traffic per pod once the breaker closed, with a three-pod minimum
about 1 microsecond of overhead per request for Cinnamon

prerequisiteReasons.rate-limiting: Circuit breakers take from rate limiting the idea of refusing some calls on purpose to protect a system that has limited capacity.

points: Consistent hashing puts servers and keys on one ring, so when a server joins or leaves only the keys next to it move.
A ring with few servers spreads load unevenly unless each server takes many points on it.
Cloudflare checked the default number of virtual nodes per server against the math, because small per-server costs become huge at fleet scale.
Discord found that on a hot read path, copying shared data can cost more than the work itself.

figures.label: Across 100 servers, load variation fell from about 99% to about 8%
over 100 TB of RAM reclaimed across the fleet

prerequisiteReasons.caching: Consistent hashing takes from caching the question of which server holds a key, and the cost of a mass reshuffle when servers change.
